extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing submissions to COLING 2025 (NLP/CL community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting long/short papers to COLING 2025, including formatting, mandatory sections, anonymity, supplementary materials, and the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits for long and short papers
rubrics_metrics.description: COLING 2025 invites the submission of long papers of up to eight pages and short papers of up to four pages. These page limits only apply to the main body of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page limits apply to the main body only; references and appendices are unlimited. Choose long vs short format appropriately and ensure the main body does not exceed the stated pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory limitations section
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the paper (after the conclusions but before the references) papers need to include a mandatory section discussing the limitations of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitations section is required and must appear between conclusions and references. It should explicitly discuss weaknesses, scope limits, and any constraints of the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional ethical considerations section
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers may optionally include a section discussing ethical considerations (positioned after conclusions and before references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, include an ethical considerations section in the same location as the limitations section; this is optional but encouraged where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlimited references and appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers can include unlimited pages of references and an unlimited appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While references and appendices are unlimited, essential details that reviewers need to assess correctness should not be relegated solely to non-main-body material (see self-contained requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use COLING 2025 style files
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should follow the general instructions for COLING 2025 proceedings and use the COLING 2025 style files (LaTeX, Word, Overleaf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates are provided; prepare your submission using the provided style files. Deviating from supplied style files is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style noncompliance leads to rejection without review
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers deviating from the provided style files will be rejected without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict enforcement: failure to adhere to the templates/formats can cause immediate desk rejection. Confirm formatting before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of ACL Ethics Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: COLING 2025 adopts the ACL Ethics Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure submissions conform to the ACL Ethics Policy; ethical expectations and requirements follow that policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission routes (Direct and ARR)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two routes for paper submission: Direct submission via Softconf/START, and committing papers previously reviewed through ACL Rolling Review (ARR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct-submitted papers follow the normal COLING review process. ARR papers can be committed to COLING 2025 and will not be re-reviewed; acceptance decisions for ARR commits will be based on ARR reviews and meta-reviews judged by Senior Area Chairs and Program Chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process: minimum reviews, rebuttal, double-blind, privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper will receive a minimum of three reviews. Authors will have the opportunity to provide a short rebuttal. The review process will be double-blind. Reviews and submissions will not be made publicly visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect at least three independent reviews; prepare a concise rebuttal to clarify misunderstandings. Ensure submissions are anonymized (see anonymization guidance for supplementary materials). Confidentiality: reviews and submissions remain private.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials: allowed formats and anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: Each COLING 2025 submission can be accompanied by a single .tgz or .zip archive containing supplementary materials, such as program code and datasets. For the main track, the supplementary materials need to be fully anonymized to preserve the double-blind reviewing policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only one archive (.tgz or .zip). Use supplementary materials to improve reproducibility. Ensure all files in the archive are fully anonymized (no author names, institutional identifiers, or other revealers) for main-track submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix and supplementary-place guidance; self-contained submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information, such as preprocessing decisions, model parameters or proofs should be put into the appendix of the main PDF submission. Note that submissions need to remain fully self-contained. In particular, any details that are important for reviewers to assess the technical correctness of the work should be included in the main body of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put supplementary methodological details in the paper's appendix (which is part of the PDF) rather than relying solely on external archives. Ensure the main submission contains all elements necessary for a reviewer to judge technical correctness; do not hide essential details in external supplement that reviewers may not inspect.
